Reviewer recommends rejection: Almost every factual claim checks out against the fetched sources. Dates, ages, titles, records, awards and the private-life details all match. I am rejecting for these fixes: (1) Delete or reword 'The hardest major to win was the French Open'. CNN only says it was the one Slam that had eluded him, and the style guide bars unattributed opinion. Also drop or source 'The awards were as steady as the results'. (2) Add the 2026 International Tennis Hall of Fame induction, which the ATP gallery from Aug 2026 reports. Cite atp-bio-hof or ithf-class-2026, and say so in the summary or body. The page is dated Oct 2026 and currently reads as if it never happened. (3) Date the foundation figures ('more than 1 million children, $50 million') as the ATP bio stated them, or check them against the foundation's own site. They are undated and may be stale. (4) The 'still stand' wording on the Grand Slam streaks rests on an ATP block marked updated 1 May 2025. Say 'according to the ATP' or add an as-of date. (5) The olympics-hof source was unreachable. Verify it or remove it, and drop any source that is not used.

claims.claim: Born 8 August 1981 in Basel, Switzerland; Swiss nationality (person.json facts, summary, FAQ)
claims.note: Britannica quick facts give the birth date and place and call him a Swiss tennis player. The ATP bio gives a Swiss father and Basel as his hometown.

claims.claim: Aged 45 in October 2026
claims.note: 8 Aug 1981 to 26 Oct 2026 is 45 years. The article's other ages also check out: 27 in June 2009 and 41 on 15 Sep 2022.

claims.claim: Ballboy in Basel in 1993-94; later won that event 10 times; 75 matches won in Basel; Basel title record
claims.note: The ATP bio says ballboy 1993-94, 10 titles and 75 matches at Basel. It also lists Basel (10) among the tournament records.

claims.claim: Retirement letter quote about 'the dreams of a young Swiss ball kid come true'
claims.note: The quote is verbatim in the full text on Scroll.

claims.claim: 20 Grand Slam singles titles: 6 Australian Open, 1 French Open, 8 Wimbledon, 5 US Open; first man to 20 majors in 2018; record eight Wimbledons; playing career 1998-2022; Olympic doubles gold 2008 and singles silver 2012
claims.note: All of this appears in Britannica's quick facts and meta description. The retirement statement and NBC piece support that he played his last match in 2022.

claims.claim: Parents Robert (Swiss) and Lynette (South African), sister Diana; started playing at 8; idols Edberg, Becker, Sampras; speaks English, French, German and Swiss German
claims.note: All appear in the ATP bio bullets.

claims.claim: 2009 French Open final: beat Soderling 6-1 7-6 6-4; aged 27; 19th Slam final; first 13 titles elsewhere; Soderling 23rd seed had beaten four-time champion Nadal; spectator incident with the cap; lost next game to love; tie-break won with four aces from four serves
claims.note: Every detail matches the CNN report.

claims.claim: Tied Sampras on 14 majors; sixth man to win all four Slams after Perry, Budge, Laver, Emerson and Agassi; Agassi presented the trophy and Federer wept; quotes 'probably my greatest ever victory' and 'with my mind at peace' on Court Philippe Chatrier; Soderling called him the best player in history
claims.note: CNN lists five earlier men, so 'sixth' is a correct count. The quotes match.

claims.claim: ATP Grand Slam records: 10 finals, 23 SFs and 36 QFs in a row; 41-match win streak 2006-07; 65 straight wins on grass 2003-08; Halle (10) and Cincinnati (7) tournament records; Wimbledon record
claims.note: All figures match the ATP bio. 'Still stand' relies on a block marked updated 1 May 2025, but nothing I found contradicts it.

claims.claim: 103 titles and 1,251 wins, second in the Open Era to Connors (109 and 1,274); never retired in 1,526 singles and 224 doubles matches; 237 consecutive weeks at No. 1, the longest in ATP Rankings history
claims.note: Matches the ATP bio exactly.

claims.claim: Laureus Sportsman of the Year five times (2005-08, 2018); Edberg Sportsmanship Award 2004-09 and 2011-17; ATP Fans' Favourite 2003-21; Comeback Player of the Year 2017
claims.note: Names, years and categories match the ATP bio.

claims.claim: Left knee surgery Feb 2016; missed six months July 2016 to Jan 2017; right knee surgeries Feb 2020, May 2020, Aug 2021; only five tournaments Feb 2020 to Aug 2022
claims.note: Matches the ATP bio. 'The injuries began in earnest in 2016' is the article's own framing, but it fits the dates.

claims.claim: Announced retirement on 15 Sep 2022 aged 41; three years of injuries and surgeries; more than 1,500 matches over 24 years; Laver Cup in London the following week was his last ATP event; 'Tennis has treated me more generously than I ever would have dreamt'; will play more tennis but not in Slams or on tour
claims.note: All in the statement dated 15 September 2022. London and 'next week' are stated in it.

claims.claim: Called Nadal after the US Open; told Trevor Noah on The Daily Show it was a very emotional call; asked for 'one last doubles'; knee 'not so good anymore'; Nadal said 'whatever it takes'; Nadal about to be a father
claims.note: All match the NBC/AP piece. 'Not totally sure' is paraphrased fairly.

claims.claim: 23 Sep 2022 lost to Sock and Tiafoe 4-6 7-6 11-9; farewell with Nadal, Murray, Djokovic, Tsitsipas, Ruud and Borg; Federer and Nadal gripping hands in tears; glad to be in tennis clothes rather than a suit
claims.note: Matches. The 23 September date comes from NBC's reference to 'Sept. 23'.

claims.claim: Wife Mirka Vavrinec, WTA career-high No. 76; first kiss at 2000 Sydney Olympics where Federer finished fourth; 2002 Hopman Cup mixed doubles 1-2; two sets of twins; four children thanked in retirement letter
claims.note: Matches the ATP bio and the letter. The word 'former' player is not in the source but is harmless. The first-kiss detail is private life, though it is published by the ATP.

claims.claim: Roger Federer Foundation founded 2003; reaches Southern Africa (Zambia, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Botswana, South Africa) and Switzerland; more than 1 million children and more than $50 million
claims.note: The ATP bio says exactly this and the article attributes it to the ATP. The figure is undated and may be stale. I did not find a foundation page to compare it with.

claims.claim: Cape Town exhibition vs Nadal on 7 Feb 2020: 51,954 spectators, $3.5m raised for the foundation, first tennis appearance in his mother's home country; $250,000 bushfire relief with Nadal in January 2020
claims.note: Matches the ATP bio, which describes it as his tennis debut in his mother's native country.

claims.claim: Swiss stamp in 2007 and coin in 2020, first living person to receive either; honorary doctorate from the University of Basel medical faculty on 24 Nov 2017; 'The Federer Express' tram in 2021
claims.note: Matches the ATP bio.

claims.note: Each is backed by the body and sources above. The metaDescription says Federer 'played his last match beside Nadal', which NBC confirms.
